findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, exposing the MySQL database directly to the internet and significantly increasing attack surface for a resource holding sensitive application data.
storage_encrypted is explicitly set to false, meaning the database storage (including credentials and any employee data) is not encrypted at rest.

The database password is supplied via var.password and referenced directly in the resource; combined with lifecycle ignore_changes on password, this indicates poor secret handling with no use of a managed secret store.

The EC2 user_data script embeds the database password (var.password) and connection details in cleartext, which is stored in instance metadata/launch configuration and readable by anyone with access to describe the instance or the metadata service, exposing DB credentials.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource '*', giving the EC2 instance role full administrative access to three core services far beyond what a catalog web app needs, violating least privilege and enabling privilege escalation if the instance is compromised.

Ingress on port 3306 is allowed from the entire VPC CIDR block rather than being scoped to only the application server's security group; combined with publicly_accessible=true on the DB, this widens the effective exposure of the database.
